title: Integrate ordinary annotation retention
evidence_required: FT-010-AC-004 RED: annotation rows are not part of the existing 90-day cleanup and can outlive their Attempt context; GREEN: diagnostics deletes them before owner confirmation without changing the promoted subset; decisive comparison: disposable old/equal/new annotated Attempts across cleanup and one safe rerun; artifact: redacted evidence under .tasks/TASK-099-T3-FT-010-W2/.

Ground-Truth Annotations Ordinary Annotation Removal RED: the existing explicit ordinary-evidence removal clears evidence but not future annotation rows; GREEN: the same diagnostics-owned transition deletes those rows and remains an idempotent no-op when repeated; decisive comparison: one disposable annotated Attempt before removal, after removal and after one repeat; artifact: redacted evidence under .tasks/TASK-099-T3-FT-010-W2/.
purpose: Delete ordinary annotation rows whenever the existing diagnostics owner expires or explicitly removes their ordinary Attempt context.
success_outcome: Scheduled expiry and explicit ordinary removal both delete annotation rows while preserving the promoted subset and their existing state/result contracts.
anti_goals: Do not implement annotation promotion, a public ordinary-removal route, Calibration selection/UI, a second cleanup command/timer, jobs/history, tombstones or production activation.
Do not add an annotation-specific cutoff or let annotation creation time extend the core Attempt lifetime.
Do not change the latest-result schema, delete promo rows directly or touch production/operator data.

forbidden_scope: Production PostgreSQL/MinIO, operator/default Attempts/evidence/annotations and real participant names
Promoted-subset creation/deletion behavior, direct diagnostics mutation of promo rows and ownership-crossing cascades
Annotation HTML routes, Calibration runs/recommendations/UI, serving settings and unrelated event/Photo retention
stop_conditions: Ordinary annotation expiry cannot reuse the existing promo-selected Attempt cutoff and diagnostics-before-promo owner order.
Scheduled expiry and explicit ordinary removal cannot share one diagnostics-owned annotation deletion boundary.
Either removal path cannot preserve the existing promoted subset while deleting ordinary annotation rows.
Safe rerun would require a new lifecycle, cleanup command, history/jobs table or cross-owner transaction.
T3 destructive probes cannot use fixed-time disposable rows, known initial state, safe rerun, synthetic names, redacted artifacts and complete cleanup.

constraints: Reuse the existing promo-selected 90-day Attempt cutoff, diagnostics-before-promo owner order and one latest-result shape; add no annotation count or scheduler state.
Use one diagnostics-owned annotation deletion boundary from scheduled expiry and explicit ordinary removal; delete rows before either operation confirms completion.
Scheduled expiry deletes annotations for every supplied Attempt even when no diagnostic_evidence row exists.
Preserve promoted_subset unchanged on both paths.
Use disposable annotated rows with one safe rerun per path and complete task-owned cleanup.
invariants: Diagnostics deletes only its ordinary evidence/annotation rows and promo deletes only confirmed promo-owned state; no cascade or direct foreign write crosses ownership.
Annotation creation or correction time never extends the core Attempt cutoff.
Neither ordinary-removal path deletes or reconstructs the curated promoted snapshot.
A repeated scheduled or explicit removal is safe and does not restore removed data or change existing state/result contracts.
verification_targets: Fixed-cutoff fixtures prove old annotation deletion including a no-evidence-row Attempt, equal/newer preservation and one safe cleanup rerun.
One explicit-removal fixture proves annotation deletion and idempotent repeat while promoted_subset remains unchanged.
Source inspection proves reuse of the existing operations with no public route, new scheduler, history, tombstone, cascade, Calibration UI or serving mutation.
